title: Leo Feist and being told to stay away from New York offices
summary: They sing and play two hours at the Leo Feist music publisher, whose manager tells them not to return to the manager's office.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So we go to the house, open up the trunk, take out our roller skates -- but I didn't tell you, this fella when we got to New York -- forgot to tell you that the man took us the next day down to Leo Feist, the biggest music publisher in New York City. He took us to Leo Feist on 7th Avenue between 47th and 46th -- 48th I think, on 7th Avenue. He took us there to let them hear who it is it was that they brought back to New York. They had a lot of entertainers there, singing songs, learning songs and so forth, that's a regular place to learn songs, Leo Feist, biggest music publisher in New York. Okay? So we must have sang for about two hours, played piano for about two hours. When we finished we met the manager of this music publishers and all, and he told us he was taking us back to 41st Street to tell us don't go back there no more

unless he tells us, unless he takes us. Okay.
This is the beginning. Kids are not allowed around New York. Understand? September 1919. Would you believe that I walked out of this man's office, about three months later after he said that, I done play Staten Island, come to his office to get the money, he raised his hand, walked out of the office and for the first time about three months later I walked back -- get your roller skates -- put our skates on, I said, Buck, put your skates on good, man because you're going to skate a while. So we put them on and we went up to 7th Avenue and they got the third rail in the middles, so we're not used to the third rail, boy we got to get used to it today cause we got to jump the third rail. That means three rails I got to cross on roller skates.
